category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Refusal to provide itemized deduction statement
expected: Explains that deductions require verified bills/receipts; tenant can challenge arbitrary deductions.
prompt: Landlord deducted ₹20,000 but refuses to give receipts or bills for the alleged repairs.
raw_response:
Hello! I understand how frustrating it is when a landlord makes unauthorized deductions from your hard-earned security deposit without providing proper proof or receipts.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant in India whose landlord has arbitrarily deducted ₹20,000 from your security deposit for alleged repairs without providing any bills or receipts. This dispute involves the return of your rightful funds and the transparency of deductions made at the end of your tenancy.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only required to restore the property in as good a condition as it was at the start, subject strictly to reasonable wear and tear. A landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or painting without explicit contractual terms or verified proof of actual damage.
- Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and corresponding state enactments) Section 11 and Section 13, security deposits must be refunded upon taking over vacant possession, minus only valid, documented deductions agreed upon in the tenancy agreement. 
- Furthermore, under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a tenant is protected against unlawful withholding of property or deposits outside due legal process.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather all available evidence, including your original rent agreement, move-in and move-out photographs or videos, and chat history or communication records where the landlord refuses to share repair bills.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to the landlord granting 15 days to either provide genuine repair bills or refund the full deducted amount of ₹20,000.
3. If the landlord fails to respond or refund the amount, approach the appropriate local Rent Authority or Consumer Commission for dispute resolution.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. Do you have a written rent agreement that specifies the rules regarding security deposit deductions?
2. What is the city or state where this rented property is located?

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
